title: Padlock journal — SOC2 scratch notes (draft)
content:
Quick purpose
- personal scratchpad for control hypotheses and evidence hunting. Not polished.
- focus angle: how inference runtime behaviour (caching, fallback, quantization) maps to SOC2 operational controls.

Topline risks I want to remember
- secret leakage via client API keys left in logs or debug dumps (low prob but critical)
- drift in model fallback policies causing different data exposure profiles when routed to different model variants
- misconfigured private deployments (VPCs) accidentally exposing management plane or metrics endpoints
- audit gaps: lack of single source of truth for who changed rollout policies or autoscale rules

Quick control mapping ideas (working)
A. Access control (logical):
  - Control hypothesis: API keys, service roles, and console UI must be RBAC enforced; emergency keys must be time-limited.
  - Evidence candidates: IAM policy snapshots, last 6 months of key creation logs (console), slack approvals for emergency keys, e2e of key rotation script in infra repo.
  - Notes: Need a reproducible query to pull "create_key" events from our event store (ELK). TODO: write the query and save as saved-search.

B. Change management (model rollouts & runtime config):
  - Hypothesis: model rollouts (canary, A/B) are described in the rollout service config and each rollout must have a ticket + mandatory reviewer.
  - Evidence: rollout config git history + PR linked to Jira ticket; rollout start/stop events in trace logs; canary metrics snapshot (latency/cost/error) stored in console.
  - Gap: auto-rollbacks currently trigger but we lack clear recorded rationale in some incidents older than Oct 2025. Need to assemble incident-notes.

C. Logging & monitoring (observability):
  - Hypothesis: token-level cost/latency logs are retained at least 90 days, with alerts for anomalies.
  - Evidence: retention policy config, example S3 lifecycle, Grafana dashboard snapshots, alert runbooks.
  - Operational nuance: we aggregate to per-route for privacy, full token-level raw logs are blue/green encrypted. Confirm encryption scheme + key rotation frequency.

D. Data protection (input/output handling):
  - Hypothesis: customer inputs stored only when explicitly enabled (debug mode) and must be labeled and access-restricted.
  - Evidence: storage buckets with labels, access ACLs, sample debug file with redaction markers, private deployment default = off.
  - TODO: confirm default debug flag in code path (hosted API config), get a code pointer.

E. Private deployments & network (unique angle)
  - Concern: VPC connectors, host firewall rules, and management plane reachability. For customer-managed deployments, we need clear docs describing responsibilities (Redwood vs customer).
  - Evidence: private-deployments runbook, customer-deployment checklist, examples of firewall rules we ask customers to apply.
  - Action: pull 3 customer deployment checklists and mark differences. Might be variation with on-prem appliances vs cloud-hosted VPC.

Evidence hunting plan (concrete steps)
- IAM key timeline: write saved ELK query, export 6 months csv, attach. (owner: Rohan)
- Rollout PR mapping: grep rollout-service repo for 'canary' + find PR->Jira linkage. (owner: Marta)
- Encryption/key rotation: ping infra-kms owner for rotation cadence (Aisha).
- Debug bucket access: list ACLs in staging and prod buckets and screenshot. (owner: Rohan)
- Private-deploy runbooks: collect three examples; annotate differences. (owner: Rohan)

Open questions / things to ask on Slack (#trust-ops)
- Are we retaining request payloads for any hosted-customer by default? I thought debug-only, but Ops said some early accounts had opt-in default turned on. Who has the list?
- Who is the owner of the 'rollout-service' DB schema? Need point of contact for extracting historical rollout events.
- Where do on-prem audit logs get forwarded? Do customers forward to our syslog endpoint or keep locally?

Short snippets — copyable for notes / ticket description
"We need to produce a 90-day artifact set for rollouts: {(1) git history of rollout config, (2) PR->ticket linkage, (3) metric snapshots pre/post canary, (4) rollback rationale if triggered}."

Quick TODO (sprint-friendly)
- [ ] Saved ELK searches for key/create, key/delete, key-rotate (due: 2026-03-12)
- [ ] Inventory of customers with debug flag ever enabled (due: 2026-03-16)
- [ ] Runbook: how to produce encrypted logs archive for audit (owner: Rohan; draft due: 2026-03-20)
- [ ] Ask infra-kms for rotation cert (owner: Aisha; due: 2026-03-10)

Random heuristics & shorthand (notes to self)
- When mapping control -> artifact, prefer "single command to produce evidence" (scripts are ❤️).
- If evidence requires human explanation (Slack thread), capture permalink and a one-line summary.
- Avoid attaching full request-level data to tickets; attach hashed/trimmed example + pointer to S3 location.

Brainstorm: possible audit-friendly improvements (low-effort wins)
- Add a small metadata header to every rollout PR template that includes "ticket:, owner:, canary-metric:, rollback-threshold:" — makes evidence assembly trivial.
- Exporter job that packages last-90-day rollout events into a zip with a manifest (git sha, metrics snapshot links).
- A 'debug-cookie' expirer that automatically turns off debug storage 7 days after first log.

References / links I keep hitting
- Confluence: SOC2 Prep Index (see linked_artifacts)
- Infra PR that added canary telemetry: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/218
- Slack thread about debug-storage opt-in: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C12345/p1678839

End notes / mental model
- Goal: controls should be provable via scripts and short human notes, not long manual hunts. That saves audit time and keeps workloads safe.
- Keep this doc informal; will extract a cleaner 'evidence playbook' after the first full assembly.

Signature
Rohan
